title: Amit Shah offers special session of Parliament on SIR if Congress writes to PM
dek: The Home Minister answered Rahul Gandhi's debate challenge at a Karnal rally, as BJP ministers and opposition parties took the fight over the voter-roll revision to the streets in several states.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday that the government was ready to call a special session of Parliament to debate the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, if the Congress formally asks for one. His offer, made at a BJP rally in Karnal, Haryana, was a reply to Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi's repeated challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an open public debate.

The exchange came on a day when both sides took the fight over the voter-roll revision to the streets. Union ministers and BJP leaders defended the exercise at marches and press conferences in at least seven states, while the Congress and Left parties held a protest in Bengaluru demanding that the SIR be scrapped and that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign. The Congress had not formally responded to Shah's offer by early Friday.

## What Shah said

Shah was speaking during the BJP's "Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao" (save democracy, remove anarchy) foot march in Karnal. "We are ready to convene a special session of Parliament to discuss the SIR exercise," he said, according to IBTimes India's translation. "If you want a discussion, just write a letter to the Prime Minister."

He said Parliament, not rallies, was the place for the debate, and accused Gandhi of disrupting proceedings and staging walkouts instead of taking part. "Let's face each other head-on," he said. "But you won't be able to handle the answers; as always, you will just run away." He also rejected the opposition's argument that the revision explains its electoral defeats: "Where was the SIR in 2014? You were completely wiped out even then," he said, adding that there had been no SIR in 2024 either.

Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, who joined the march, accused the Congress of spreading lies and said periodic revisions keep voter lists accurate, according to a report carried by WebIndia123.

## The challenge Shah was answering

Gandhi first challenged Modi to a debate on Monday, in a post on X accusing him of holding office with "foreign help" and offering to debate "any stage, any time". The BJP dismissed the charge at the time. At an "Insaaf Rally" in Sangrur, Punjab, on Wednesday, Gandhi renewed the challenge, WebIndia123 reported. At the INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally in Delhi on 1 November, he accused the Chief Election Commissioner of facilitating "vote theft".

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, on Wednesday, urged Modi to accept the debate and answer questions on alleged "vote chori", the Election Commission's handling of the SIR, and the government's claim that about three crore people found during the revision were infiltrators, The Tribune reported. If the claim was true, Kharge asked, what had the Home Minister been doing while so many people entered illegally. "He should be sacked for his incompetence," Kharge said. He also accused the Commission of making five "U-turns" during the exercise, including changes to Form 6, the form used to register new voters.

## What each side said on Thursday

On the government side, according to WebIndia123:

- Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav, speaking in Darbhanga and Patna, said rolls had been revised eight times since 1950 and this was the ninth. He said the revision removes dead voters, people who have moved and duplicate entries, and that only two objections were filed although draft lists went to 1,60,813 booth-level agents.
- Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, in Jaipur, said the government was ready to facilitate a debate and accused the Congress of walking out of Parliament.
- BJP MP Sambit Patra, in Bengaluru, said leaders should debate in Parliament, not on the streets.
- Union Minister of State Nityanand Rai, in Surat, said the SIR aims to include every eligible citizen and accused the Congress of shielding infiltrators.
- Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that demanding answers meant listening to the government's reply.

On the opposition side:

- At Freedom Park in Bengaluru, the Congress, the CPI(M), the CPI, the CPI(ML) Liberation, the Forward Bloc, the Samajwadi Party and other groups protested from 11 am to 2 pm. Former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah demanded that the SIR be scrapped and the CEC resign. He said Karnataka's electorate fell from about 5.54 crore to 4.55 crore after the revision, a figure The Declaration could not independently check.
- Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said voters wrongly deleted, other than those who had died, deserved justice. State Congress chief B K Hariprasad said the protest would continue until the CEC resigns.
- CPI(M) MP John Brittas said the opposition had asked for a debate on the SIR at an all-party meeting chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and the government had refused. CPI(M) leader Hannan Mollah said opposition microphones had been switched off in Parliament.
- Congress leader Bhai Jagtap, in Mumbai, welcomed the challenge and said a debate should also cover unemployment and inflation.

## Background

The SIR is the Election Commission's house-to-house re-verification of voter lists, in which electors have to establish their eligibility afresh. It began in Bihar in 2025 and has since been carried out in several other states, including West Bengal. In Bengal, a separate special summary revision of the rolls is now under way before the Kolkata and Howrah civic elections, and the Trinamool Congress, the Congress and the Left have objected to new rules for deleting names. The opposition says it is being used to delete genuine voters, especially the poor, migrants and minorities. The government and the Commission say it removes ineligible names and that every eligible citizen can be included.

The row has hardened since late October. On 31 October INDIA bloc leaders staged a symbolic "public impeachment" of CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Kharge's residence, after notices for a formal removal motion were rejected in Parliament earlier this year. The next day the bloc held its rally at Ramlila Maidan. Separately, the Supreme Court has issued notice on a petition challenging the legal immunity given to the CEC and Election Commissioners.

## What happens next

A special session needs the government to summon Parliament; Shah's condition is that the Congress first writes to the Prime Minister. The Congress has not said whether it will. The Winter Session would normally begin in late November or early December, but dates have not been announced. Karnataka Congress leaders say their protest will move to districts, taluks and blocks, and the BJP's marches continue.
